mcq.q: Which word makes a request polite?
mcq.explanation: Please turns an order into a polite request.

mcq.q: What do we say when someone thanks us?
mcq.explanation: You are welcome is the polite reply.

mcq.q: Which phrase do we use to get someone's attention politely?
mcq.explanation: Excuse me is polite.

mcq.q: Which is a minimal pair for /p/ and /b/?
mcq.explanation: Pig and big differ only in the first sound.

mcq.q: Which word has the vowel /eɪ/?
mcq.explanation: Wait has /eɪ/, but wet, pen and bed have /e/.

mcq.q: Which word has the vowel /e/?
mcq.explanation: Bed has the short vowel /e/.

mcq.q: What do we say when a friend wins a prize?
mcq.explanation: Congratulations shows we are happy for someone.

mcq.q: Which is the more polite request?
options: May I borrow your pen, please?
mcq.explanation: It uses may I and please.

mcq.q: When do we say 'I beg your pardon'?
options: When we did not hear or we need to say sorry
mcq.explanation: It asks a person to repeat or says sorry.

mcq.q: Which is a greeting for the afternoon?
mcq.explanation: Good afternoon is used after midday.

mcq.q: /p/ is a whispered sound. /b/ is
mcq.explanation: The difference between p and b is the voice.

mcq.q: Which pair is a minimal pair for /e/ and /eɪ/?
mcq.explanation: Let and late differ in the vowel sound.

mcq.q: To scan a text means to
mcq.explanation: Scanning is used to find a name, number or word.

mcq.q: To skim a text means to
options: read quickly to get the main idea
mcq.explanation: Skimming gives you the general idea.

mcq.q: A factual question has an answer that
mcq.explanation: Factual answers can be found in the words of the passage.

mcq.q: An inferential question needs you to
mcq.explanation: Inference means working out the answer from clues.

mcq.q: In 'The Purse in the Market', what did Neema do with the purse?
options: She returned it to its owner
mcq.explanation: Neema found the woman and returned the purse.

mcq.q: Which word best describes Neema in the passage?
mcq.explanation: She returned the purse and refused a reward.

mcq.q: 'She sighed with relief' means she
options: was happy that a worry was over
mcq.explanation: Relief is the feeling when a worry ends.

mcq.q: What is a good way to find the meaning of an unknown word in a passage?
options: Read the sentences around it for clues
mcq.explanation: Context clues help you understand new words.

mcq.q: Which is the best first step before answering a question on a passage?
options: Read the question and find key words
mcq.explanation: Key words tell you what to look for in the text.

mcq.q: Why did the woman say Neema's mother had taught her good manners?
options: Because Neema spoke and acted politely
mcq.explanation: Her actions showed good manners.

mcq.q: We answer comprehension questions best in
mcq.explanation: Full sentences show that we understand.

mcq.q: Reading a text again more slowly to understand it well is called
mcq.explanation: Intensive reading means careful, slow reading.

mcq.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: We have chairs enough to sit on.
We have enough chair to sit on.
We have enough chairs for sit.
We have enough chairs to sit on.
mcq.explanation: The pattern is enough + noun + to + verb.

mcq.q: In the pattern 'enough + noun + to + verb', the word after 'to' is a
mcq.explanation: To is followed by a verb such as sit or eat.

mcq.q: Which sentence uses 'a lot of' correctly?
options: There are a lot children in the yard.
There are a lot of children in the yard.
There are lot of children in the yard.
There are alot of children in the yard.
mcq.explanation: A lot of is written as three words and is followed by a noun.

mcq.q: 'She reads a lot.' Here 'a lot' means
mcq.explanation: A lot at the end of a sentence tells how much or how often.

mcq.q: Which is correct?
options: There is water enough to drink.
There is enough water for drink.
There enough is water to drink.
There is enough water to drink.
mcq.explanation: Enough comes before the noun.

mcq.q: Which is a negative sentence?
options: I do not have enough money to buy a bicycle.
mcq.explanation: It says that the money is not sufficient.

mcq.q: 'He is old enough to ride a bicycle.' Here enough comes
mcq.explanation: With adjectives, enough comes after the adjective.

mcq.q: Which is correct spelling?
mcq.explanation: A lot is two words.

mcq.q: Which sentence has a lot of a noun we cannot count?
options: We have a lot of cows.
We have a lot of chairs.
We have a lot of pupils.
We have a lot of rain in April.
mcq.explanation: Rain cannot be counted.

mcq.q: Complete: 'Mother bought enough flour ___ chapati.'
mcq.explanation: Use to + verb.

mcq.q: Which question uses the pattern correctly?
options: Do we enough have chairs to seat the guests?
Do we have enough chairs to seat the guests?
Have we chairs enough to seat guests?
Enough chairs do we to seat the guests?
mcq.explanation: Enough comes before the noun chairs.

mcq.q: Which letter is a tail letter?
mcq.explanation: G hangs below the line.

mcq.q: Which letter is a tall letter?
mcq.explanation: H reaches the top line.

mcq.q: Which letter is silent in 'knife'?
mcq.explanation: We say nife, so the k is silent.

mcq.q: Which letter is silent in 'write'?
mcq.explanation: We say rite, so the w is silent.

mcq.q: Which word has a silent b?
mcq.explanation: In lamb the b is not pronounced.

mcq.q: Which word has a double consonant?
mcq.explanation: Dinner has double n.

mcq.q: What should you use first when learning neat print script?
mcq.explanation: A pencil allows you to rub out mistakes.

mcq.q: Which describes the letter b?
options: A round part with the stick on its right
A stick with the round part on its right
A stick that goes below the line
mcq.explanation: For b the stick is on the left and the round part on the right.

mcq.q: Why should there be a gap between words?
options: So that the words are easy to read
mcq.explanation: Gaps make the writing legible.

mcq.q: Which word has a silent h at the start?
mcq.explanation: Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the h is silent.

mcq.q: Which word contains the blend 'tr'?
mcq.explanation: Train begins with t and r.

mcq.q: In 'listen', the silent letter is
mcq.explanation: We say lisn, so the t is silent.

short.q: Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate.
short.answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
short.working: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

short.q: Write two minimal pairs for /p/ and /b/.
short.answer: For example: pin, bin and pat, bat.

short.q: Name three polite words or phrases and say when each is used.
short.answer: Please: when asking. Thank you: when someone helps. Sorry: when we make a mistake.
short.working: 1 mark for each phrase with its use.

short.q: Why is it important to use polite words? Give two reasons.
short.answer: Polite words show respect and make people feel welcome. They help people to cooperate and be friendly.

short.q: Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely.
short.answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
short.working: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

short.q: State the difference between a factual question and an inferential question.
short.answer: A factual question has an answer stated in the text. An inferential question needs you to use clues and think.

short.q: In the passage 'The Purse in the Market', what did the purse contain?
short.answer: It had some coins and a card with the name Mrs Achieng Odhiambo.
short.working: 1 mark for the coins and 1 mark for the card.

short.q: Explain what we learn from the story about honesty.
short.answer: Honesty means returning what belongs to others. Neema returned the purse and refused a reward, and her mother said honesty is a great treasure.
short.working: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for the message.

short.q: Describe how to skim and how to scan a passage.
short.answer: To skim, look at the title, pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph to get the main idea. To scan, look quickly for key words to find a particular fact.
short.working: 2 marks for skimming and 2 marks for scanning.

short.q: Complete the sentences: (a) We have enough plates ___ (eat) the meal. (b) There is enough rice ___ (feed) the guests.
Correct these sentences: (a) 'I have money enough to buy bread.' (b) 'She has alot of friends.'
short.answer: (a) I have enough money to buy bread. (b) She has a lot of friends.

short.q: Write one sentence with 'enough ... to' and one with 'a lot of' about your school.
short.answer: We have enough desks to seat every learner. The school has a lot of trees.
short.working: 1 mark for each pattern and 1 mark for correct punctuation.

short.q: Explain the difference in position of 'enough' with a noun and with an adjective. Give an example of each.
short.answer: With a noun, enough comes before it: enough food. With an adjective, enough comes after it: tall enough.
short.working: 1 mark for each position and 1 mark for each example.

short.q: Write three tall letters and three tail letters.
short.answer: Tall: b, d, h (or f, k, l, t). Tail: g, p, y (or j, q).
short.working: 1 mark for each set, up to 3, with a mark for correctness.

short.q: Copy in neat print: 'Please listen carefully.' Circle the silent letter.
short.answer: Please listen carefully. (silent t in listen)
short.working: 1 mark for neat copying and 1 mark for identifying t.

short.q: List three things that make handwriting legible.
short.answer: Letters of the correct size, letters sitting on the line, even gaps between letters and words, correct spelling.

short.q: Explain how you can tell b from d when you write.
short.answer: b: stick first then the round part on the right. d: round part first then the stick on the right.

short.q: Write four words with double consonants and four words with blends.
short.answer: Double: letter, dinner, apple, bottle. Blends: train, snake, clap, flag.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct group of two words, up to 4.
